response.text:
I can’t produce exact revenue numbers from that chart as described. With only unlabeled gridlines and unlabeled bars there isn’t enough information to determine exact values — I would be fabricating numbers if I gave “exact” figures. (Policy / chart-accuracy guidance: do not infer exact values from visuals without axis labels or source data.)

I can help in one of three safe ways — pick whichever works for you:

1) I’ll extract exact numbers if you can share the chart image or the source data
   - Option A: attach the image here (or paste a link to it). I can measure the bars and give best-estimate values with uncertainty, or extract exact values if the underlying data/table is available.
   - Option B: paste the underlying data table (CSV / list of numbers) if you have it.

2) If you cannot attach the file, I can give a step‑by‑step method you can follow quickly to get numeric values yourself:
   - Open the chart image in any image editor (Paint, Preview, Photoshop) that shows pixel coordinates.
   - Identify the chart plotting area vertical coordinates: y_top (top of plot area at the top gridline) and y_bottom (baseline).
   - For each month’s bar, note y_bar (the pixel y coordinate of the top of the bar).
   - Compute bar_height_pixels = y_bottom - y_bar, and full_height_pixels = y_bottom - y_top.
   - Relative height = bar_height_pixels / full_height_pixels.
   - If you know the numeric value represented by the top gridline (call it TopValue), then month_value = Relative height × TopValue.
   - If you don’t know TopValue, you must supply one (e.g., round number like $500,000) — once you give a TopValue I’ll convert the relative heights into exact numbers for each month.
   - If you want, tell me the pixel measurements and TopValue and I’ll compute immediately.

3) If you want a quick approximate set of numbers now, I can produce estimates under clearly stated assumptions
   - Example: “Assume the top gridline is $600,000 and there are 5 evenly spaced gridlines.” I’ll estimate each month’s value and provide ranges (±) and a confidence note. Tell me which TopValue and currency/unit to assume.

Which option do you prefer? If you can’t attach the image here, say whether you can paste a public link, or give the number of horizontal gridlines and whether any bar reaches the top (or baseline) and a TopValue to assume — I’ll convert that into numbers for you.
